about.what: One row per results box (contest) in the harvested Wikipedia election articles: the source to cite for it, every other source Wikipedia gives for it, and the matching Civgraph election file.

status.verified: a source Civgraph fetched contains the result
status.cited-by-wikipedia: Wikipedia gives a source for it that Civgraph could not check; cite it as cited by Wikipedia, not checked by Civgraph
status.wikipedia-only: no source found in the article; the figures are known only from Wikipedia

about.verification: >=80% of the candidates' surnames and >=60% of their first-preference votes (>=50) in one fetched document, as whole tokens.

scope.same section: cited in the section the box sits in
scope.article: cited elsewhere in the article and looks like a results source

basis.section-citation: citation template in a Sources/Bibliography list
basis.body-link: plain link in the article text
basis.inline-text: reference with no template or link

about.dropped: Sources fetched and found not to contain the contest (under 80%% of surnames) are left out.
about.relatedWikipedia: Wikipedia articles covering this contest, for provenance ("related Wikipedia articles"). Not a citation.
about.civgraph: Relative to data/elections-source/data/elections. match=exact, area-only (unique that year) or fuzzy (order-free name tokens).
about.licence: Wikipedia article text is CC BY-SA 4.0. This file lists citations (URLs and titles), not copied source content. If Civgraph takes figures from Wikipedia itself (wikipedia-only rows), that use needs attribution to the article.
